highlights.title: Coherence via kernels of maps from finite free modules
highlights.statement: For any unital, possibly noncommutative ring R and any left R-module M, M is coherent (finitely generated with every finitely generated submodule finitely presented) if and only if M is finitely generated and the kernel of every R-linear map Rⁿ → M is finitely generated for every natural number n, including zero.

highlights.title: Finiteness, projectivity and flatness under injective tensor units
highlights.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, S an R-algebra and M an additive commutative monoid with its given R-module structure. Assume the canonical unit N → S ⊗[R] N is injective for every additive commutative R-semimodule N in Type (max uR uM). For a possibly noncommutative semiring S, S ⊗[R] M is finitely generated over S if and only if M is finitely generated over R. For a possibly noncommutative ring S, the corresponding finite-presentation equivalence holds. If S ⊗[R] M is finite and projective over any possibly noncommutative semiring S, M is finite and projective over R; finite presentation of M is derived internally. For a commutative ring S, flatness is likewise equivalent. All three carrier universes are independent; S need not be flat over R, and M needs neither an S-action nor a supplied additive group structure.

highlights.title: Internal Krull–Schmidt decompositions and cancellation
highlights.statement: Over any possibly noncommutative ring, a Noetherian module or an Artinian module is a finite internal direct sum of nonzero indecomposable submodules, with an explicit A i ≠ ⊥ fact paired with each summand's categorical indecomposability. Two supplied finite internal decompositions of linearly equivalent modules have matching summands up to linear equivalence when all summands have local endomorphism rings. Indecomposable summands and finite length of one total suffice instead. Both matching conclusions include explicit nonzero facts for each supplied family. Arbitrary finite index types use the caller's decidable equality instances and may be empty; existence uses stock equality on Fin n. Matching is existential; no preservation of the given coordinates or canonical choice is asserted. A common finite-length module P, possibly zero, cancels from P × M ≃ₗ[R] P × N with no chain condition on M or N. Zero modules, including those over a zero ring, have the empty decomposition.

highlights.title: Coherence of square-zero extensions and finite-support idealizations
highlights.statement: For a division ring D and a bimodule M in independent universes, the trivial square-zero extension D ⋉ M is left coherent if and only if M is finitely generated on the left. Both compatible module actions are retained, without centrality. For the stock pointwise left module ι →₀ D and any compatible right action, this is equivalent to finiteness of ι, including the empty index type. For a field k and infinite ι, the canonical inclusion algebra k → TrivSqZeroExt k (ι →₀ k), a ↦ (a, 0), is faithfully flat but not coherent. The canonical field criterion allows the zero coefficient space; finite generation means finite dimension, not a finite underlying set. More generally, for a possibly noncommutative ring R and a bimodule M with its given commuting left and right actions, left coherence of R ⋉ M implies finite generation of M on the left whenever r ↦ r • v is injective for one vector v. Sufficiency holds for a left coherent base and a coefficient bimodule finitely presented on the left.

headlines.title: Spans, kernels and coordinate faces
headlines.text:
For a linear map of semimodules over
any possibly noncommutative semiring, if its target has no nonzero additive
summands of zero and has no zero scalar divisors, then
`span R S ⊓ ker f = span R (S ∩ ↑(ker f))` for every set `S`.
Intersecting a finitely generated submodule with this kernel remains finitely
generated. The [image-only corollaries](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Span/Kernel.lean)
require these two properties only on `range f`, without changing the kernel.
For an arbitrary coefficient module `A` with those properties and arbitrary
index and support sets, the [coordinate-face formulas](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Finsupp/Supported.lean)
give the same conclusions for `Finsupp.supported A R J`, using the given
`R`-action. The [polynomial example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesExamples/PolynomialFaces.lean)
exhibits a nonzero proper face of a two-generated semimodule over `ℕ[X]`.
If `R` is zero-sum-free and has no zero divisors, every
[uniformly degree-bounded coefficient face](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Polynomial/CoefficientFace.lean)
of a finitely generated submodule of `I →₀ R[X]` is finitely generated over
`R`. The allowed coefficient positions may correlate the index and degree;
neither `I` nor the allowed set needs to be finite. The whole polynomial
submodule need not be finitely generated over `R`, and `R` need not be
commutative.

headlines.title: Polynomial intertwining
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary semiring `S`, additive commutative
monoids `M`, `N`, and coefficient representations `σ : S →+* AddMonoid.End M`,
`τ : S →+* AddMonoid.End N`, an additive map `h : M →+ N` that intertwines
every `σ s` with `τ s` and the selected endomorphisms `f` with `g` also
intertwines their plain polynomial evaluations. The
[semilinear version](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/LinearMap/Evaluation.lean)
uses the given module structures over independent semirings `R`, `R₂`, any
scalar homomorphism `η : R →+* R₂`, an `η`-semilinear map `h`, and representations
into the respective linear endomorphism semirings. The hypotheses
`(τ s).comp h = h.comp (σ s)` for every `s` and `g.comp h = h.comp f` imply
`(p.eval₂ τ g).comp h = h.comp (p.eval₂ σ f)`. All five carrier universes
are independent. No coefficient/end commutation, finiteness, or module
structure on the semilinear Hom is required.

headlines.title: Stable kernels and ranges
headlines.text:
For an additive commutative group with its given
module structure over a possibly zero, noncommutative semiring, simultaneous
one-step stability at a natural bound, including zero, gives the specified
sum equivalence from the power kernel and range. The kernel restriction is
nilpotent and the range restriction is an automorphism. Canonical projections
are independent of the stable bound and natural for arbitrary linear
intertwiners. Noetherianity and Artinianity of the module give a common bound;
the separate Noetherian-surjective and Artinian-injective automorphism
criteria retain their asymmetric hypotheses. See
[`StableKernelRange`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/End/StableKernelRange.lean).
Over arbitrary ring scalars, a finite-length module that is categorically
indecomposable has a local endomorphism ring, and each endomorphism is
nilpotent or a unit. The indecomposable predicate already excludes the zero
module; see [`Local`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/End/Local.lean).
The classical ring-module antecedents are Fitting's lemma and its
indecomposable finite-length local-endomorphism consequence, as presented in
Wisbauer, *Foundations of Module and Ring Theory*, §§31.13 and 32.4(3)(iii).
The explicit-one-step semiring/additive-group decomposition above generalizes
the cited ring-module setting; the local-endomorphism theorem retains ring
scalars. See [references and credit](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/README.md#references-and-credit).

headlines.title: Internal Krull–Schmidt decompositions and cancellation
headlines.text:
Over any ring, a
Noetherian module or an Artinian module is a finite internal direct sum of
nonzero indecomposable submodules; the two chain conditions are separate
existence hypotheses. Each existence witness includes `A i ≠ ⊥` alongside
categorical indecomposability. Two supplied finite internal decompositions of
linearly equivalent modules match up to an equivalence of index types and
linear equivalences of summands when all summands have local endomorphism
rings. Indecomposable summands and finite length of one total give the same
matching. Both matching conclusions include `∀ i, A i ≠ ⊥` and
`∀ j, B j ≠ ⊥`, derived from the given hypotheses. Arbitrary finite index
types use the caller's decidable equality instances and may be empty;
existence uses the stock equality instance on `Fin n`. The matching is
existential, not required to preserve the given coordinates. A common
finite-length module `P` cancels from `P × M ≃ₗ[R] P × N`, with no chain
condition on `M` or `N`; `P` may be zero. Zero modules, including those over
a zero ring, have the empty decomposition. See
[`KrullSchmidt`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/KrullSchmidt.lean), which realizes
the categorical theorems of Homological Algebra through `ModuleCat`.

headlines.title: Additive intertwining by ranges
headlines.text:
An additive map between commutative monoids
intertwines a finite family of source endomorphisms summing to the identity with
an orthogonal idempotent target family if and only if it maps each source range
into its corresponding target range. No source orthogonality, target completeness,
subtraction or cancellation is required, and the monoid and index universes are
independent. The arbitrary-index range-action lemma also supplies the coordinate
calculation for the existing linear product-of-ranges equivalence through
Mathlib's canonical endomorphism action. See
[`OrthogonalIdempotents.semiconj_iff_mapsTo_range`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean)
and [`linearEquivPiRange`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/DirectSum/Idempotents.lean).

headlines.title: Fibrewise additive intertwining
headlines.text:
For additive commutative monoids `M`, `N`,
let `P : I → AddMonoid.End M` have finite index set and sum to the identity, and
let `Q : J → AddMonoid.End N` be an orthogonal idempotent family, with
decidable equality on `J`. For any `q : I → J` and additive `h : M →+ N`,
sending `range (P i)` into `range (Q (q i))` for every `i` implies
`h ∘ (∑ i with q i = j, P i) = Q j ∘ h` for every `j`. This implication uses
no source orthogonality; it is an equivalence when `P` is a complete orthogonal
idempotent family.
The target label set may be infinite, and `Q` need not be complete; labels may
be merged or omitted. An unused `Q j` need only kill `h(M)`, not vanish on all
of `N`. No subtraction, cancellation or scalar compatibility is required, and
the two monoid and two index universes are independent. See
[`OrthogonalIdempotents.semiconj_sum_fiberwise_of_mapsTo_range`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean)
and [`CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.semiconj_sum_fiberwise_iff_mapsTo_range`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean).

headlines.title: Finite coarsening of complete orthogonal idempotents
headlines.text:
Over any possibly
noncommutative `Semiring A`, summing a finite complete orthogonal family over
the fibres of an arbitrary map `q : I → J` gives a complete orthogonal family
indexed by `J`. Both index types have `Fintype` instances, with decidable equality
needed only on `J`; the three universes are independent. The map need not be
surjective: unused labels have value zero. Empty index types and zero semirings
are allowed; no additive inverses, cancellation or centrality is required. See
[`CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.sum_fiberwise`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean).

headlines.title: Dual endomorphisms
headlines.text:
Over a commutative semiring `R`,
[`Module.End.dualMapAlgHom`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Dual/End.lean)
bundles dualization as an algebra homomorphism from the opposite endomorphism
algebra of any `R`-semimodule. For a possibly noncommutative `R`-algebra `A`,
`Module.Dual.rightRegularAlgHom` gives named operators
`F_a(φ)(x) = φ(a * x)`, with `F_a.comp F_b = F_(b * a)` and the original
pointwise `R`-scalar structure on the dual. No finiteness or freeness is required.
Over a commutative ring `R` and a possibly noncommutative ring algebra `A`,
[`Module.Dual.coextensionEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Coextension.lean)
identifies opposite-algebra coextension of `R`, restricted to `R`, with the
original dual, intertwining coextension translation with these named operators.
Its generic [pointwise Hom comparison](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean)
retains the given algebra action and allows independent scalar and module universes.
For self-pairings,
[`LinearMap.nondegenerate_of_surjective_of_separatingLeft`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Nondegenerate.lean)
proves both separating directions from surjectivity and left separation;
a bijective map to the dual is consequently nondegenerate, even for semimodules.

headlines.title: Tensor–dual Frobenius criterion
headlines.text:
For a finite-dimensional, possibly
noncommutative or zero algebra `A` over a field `K`,
[`Module.Dual.exists_nondegenerate_mul_of_tensorProduct_equiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Dual/TensorProduct.lean)
produces a functional `λ` with both-sided nondegenerate pairing `λ(a * x)`
from a subspace `C` of the original dual and an equivalence
`e : C ⊗[K] A ≃ₗ[K] Module.Dual K A` satisfying
`e (c ⊗ₜ a) x = c (a * x)`. The algebra needs only `Semiring A`;
finiteness of `C` is derived, and the scalar and algebra universes are independent.

headlines.title: Annihilator quotients with two scalar actions
headlines.text:
Suppose a ring `A` and a
semiring `C` act on the same additive commutative monoid `M`, with commuting
given actions. If `M` is finitely generated over `C` and Noetherian over `A`,
then `A` modulo the annihilator of its original action is left Noetherian;
see
[`isNoetherianRing_quotient_annihilator_of_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Noetherian.lean).
If `M` is an additive commutative group, finite generation over `C` and
coherence over `A` instead give a coherent annihilator quotient, as a
regular left module over the quotient ring; see
[`isCoherentRing_quotient_annihilator_of_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Quotient.lean).
The three universes are independent. Neither scalar type needs to be
Noetherian, and the `A`-action need not commute with itself.
Taking `C = A` in the Noetherian result recovers the self-commuting criterion:
for an additive commutative group with a self-commuting `A`-action, Noetherianity over `A`
is equivalent to finite generation over `A` and left Noetherianity of the
annihilator quotient. In particular, this applies over every commutative
ring. The sufficient direction holds over any ring for an additive
commutative monoid with its given module structure, without a commutation
hypothesis.

headlines.title: Noetherian semilinear Hom
headlines.text:
For semirings `R`, `R₂`, a ring `S`, a finitely
generated `R`-semimodule `M`, and a Noetherian `S`-module `N` with a commuting
`R₂`-action,
[`isNoetherian_semilinearMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Noetherian.lean)
makes `M →ₛₗ[σ] N` Noetherian for the canonical pointwise `S`-action, for every
`σ : R →+* R₂`. The five universes are independent; no surjectivity of `σ`,
scalar commutativity or ambient Noetherianity is required.
`isNoetherian_linearMap_of_finite` gives the plain-linear specialization and
recovers Mathlib's `isNoetherian_linearMap` proposition in its commutative-ring
case, with the same pointwise action.

headlines.title: Hom and End of matrix columns
headlines.text:
Over an arbitrary possibly noncommutative
semiring `R`, finite-sum matrix actions retain the given coefficient-module
structures. For a finite nonempty index `I`,
[`LinearMap.matrixModuleHomAddEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ColumnHom.lean)
identifies coefficient-linear maps additively with matrix-linear maps of columns;
its inverse is characterized at every coordinate.
`Module.matrixModuleEndRingEquiv` preserves the usual order of composition.
For the regular coefficient module this gives `Rᵐᵒᵖ`, not the full matrix semiring.
With empty `I`, coordinate extension is still surjective, but need not be
injective. Zero semirings are allowed, and no scalar-module structure on a
general Hom is used.

headlines.title: Projective matrix-column semimodules
headlines.text:
For a semiring `R`, an additive
commutative monoid `M` with its given `R`-module structure, and a finite type `I`
with decidable equality,
[`Matrix.Module.projective_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Projective.lean)
characterizes projectivity of the canonical `Matrix I I R`-module on `I → M` by
`IsEmpty I ∨ Module.Projective R M`. In particular, for inhabited `I`, projectivity
is equivalent to that of `M` over `R`. No coefficient commutativity or additive
inverses are required, and the carrier universes are independent.

headlines.title: Left ideals of finite matrix semirings
headlines.text:
For `[Semiring R]`, `[Fintype I]`
and `[DecidableEq I]`, including empty `I`,
[`Submodule.matrixRowsOrderIso`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/RowIdeal.lean)
identifies left ideals of `Matrix I I R` with `R`-submodules of the row module
`I → R`. Left Artinianity and left Noetherianity of the matrix semiring are
equivalent to the corresponding conditions on this row module, not to
unrestricted conditions on the coefficient semiring.

headlines.title: Coherence of finite matrix rings
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary, possibly noncommutative
or zero `Ring R`, a finite type `I` with its given decidable equality, and the
canonical regular left modules,
[`Matrix.instIsCoherentRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/CoherentRing.lean)
gives coherence of `Matrix I I R` from coherence of `R`, including empty `I`.
For nonempty `I`, `IsCoherentRing.of_matrix` reflects coherence and
`Matrix.isCoherentRing_iff` gives the equivalence. The ring and index universes
are independent. The supporting
[`Matrix.entrywiseLinearMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Entrywise.lean)
applies a coefficient-linear map `(κ → R) →ₗ[R] R` entrywise to a family of
matrices, linearly for regular left matrix multiplication, over any semiring
and arbitrary family index `κ`. Its scalar-restricted kernel has a split
entry projection onto the coefficient kernel. Reflection needs nonempty `I`:
the empty matrix ring has one element and is coherent for every `R`.
More generally, for any additive commutative monoid `M` with its given
`R`-module structure,
[`Matrix.Module.instIsCoherent`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/CoherentModule.lean)
preserves coherence under the canonical finite-sum action of `Matrix I I R`
on `I → M`, including empty `I`. For nonempty `I`,
`Module.IsCoherent.of_matrixModule` reflects coherence and
`Matrix.Module.isCoherent_iff` gives the equivalence with `Module.IsCoherent R M`.
No coherence of `R`, Noetherianity, or extra finite-generation premise is
required. The index, coefficient and module universes are independent, and
`R` may be zero. With empty `I`, every column module is a subsingleton and
hence coherent, so nonemptiness is essential for reflection.

headlines.title: Left-regular elements in left Artinian rings
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary unital
`Ring A` with `[IsArtinianRing A]`,
[`IsLeftRegular.isUnit_of_isArtinianRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Artinian/Regular.lean)
makes every left-regular element a unit. Artinianity concerns the original
left regular module; no opposite-Artinian, commutativity or nontriviality
hypothesis is required, and the carrier universe is arbitrary. The reverse
implication is already available through Mathlib's `IsUnit.isRegular`.

headlines.title: Closed semimodule categories
headlines.text:
For a `CommSemiring R`,
[`SemimoduleCat.tensorLeftHomAdjunction`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Monoidal/Closed.lean)
makes tensoring with `M` left adjoint to its wrapped-morphism Hom functor.
The Hom functor allows an independent carrier universe; the monoidal closed
structure uses the common scalar and carrier universe of the tensor category.
Currying, uncurrying, evaluation and coevaluation have pure-tensor formulas.
Over a commutative ring, `ModuleCat.ihomSemimoduleIso` compares the chosen
internal Homs and their unit, counit and precomposition maps.
The [finite-basis client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Monoidal/Closed.lean)
uses a specified basis with finite index type to show that tensoring preserves
existing limits at two independent diagram sizes; the index universe is
independent as well.

headlines.title: Kernels over semirings
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary `Semiring R`,
[`SemimoduleCat.kernelIsLimit`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Kernels.lean)
makes the existing kernel submodule, with its subtype inclusion, a categorical
kernel. `SemimoduleCat.hasKernels_semimoduleCat` gives kernels in
`SemimoduleCat.{v} R`, with independent coefficient and carrier universes.
Over a ring, `ModuleCat.kernelCone_semimodule_hom_apply` shows that the
comparison with Mathlib's module kernel preserves underlying elements.

headlines.title: Sums of nilpotent left ideals
headlines.text:
For arbitrary left ideals `I`, `J` of a
possibly noncommutative `Semiring R`,
[`Ideal.sup_pow_add_sub_one_le`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Operations.lean)
gives `(I ⊔ J) ^ (m + n - 1) ≤ I ^ m * ⊤ ⊔ J ^ n * ⊤` for all natural
`m`, `n`. Global witnesses `I ^ m = 0` and `J ^ n = 0` therefore give
`(I ⊔ J) ^ (m + n - 1) = 0`; `Ideal.isNilpotent_sup` makes the sum of two
globally nilpotent left ideals nilpotent. No commutativity, two-sidedness or
positivity of the exponents is required. The
[relative-generation client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Ideal/Operations.lean)
combines this with nilpotent-ideal elimination to deduce `P ≤ N` from
`P ≤ N ⊔ (I ⊔ J) • P` in any additive commutative `R`-semimodule, with an
independent carrier universe.

headlines.title: Inverse images with nilpotent kernel
headlines.text:
For a unital semiring homomorphism `f`
and a target left ideal `J`,
[`Ideal.pow_comap_eq_zero_of_ker_pow_eq_zero`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Comap.lean)
gives `J.comap f ^ (m * n) = 0` from the global witnesses `J ^ m = 0` and
`(RingHom.ker f) ^ n = 0`. The companion `Ideal.isNilpotent_comap` gives global
nilpotence of the inverse image. Both semirings may be noncommutative, all natural
exponents including zero are allowed, and the source, target and generic
`RingHomClass` homomorphism family have independent universes. The same module
gives product and power inclusions for inverse images without nilpotence hypotheses.

headlines.title: Relative generation by nilpotent ideals
headlines.text:
For a left ideal `I` of a
possibly noncommutative semiring `R` and submodules `N`, `P` of an additive
commutative `R`-semimodule,
[`Submodule.le_sup_pow_smul_of_le_sup_smul`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Operations.lean)
propagates `P ≤ N ⊔ I • P` to `P ≤ N ⊔ (I ^ n) • P` for every natural `n`.
Under global nilpotence `IsNilpotent I`, the companion
`Submodule.le_of_le_sup_smul_of_isNilpotent` gives `P ≤ N`.
The carrier universes are independent, and no finite generation, additive
inverses, cancellation or nontriviality is required.

headlines.title: Extension of products and powers of left ideals
headlines.text:
For any unital homomorphism
`f : A →+* B` between semirings in independent universes,
[`Ideal.map_mul_of_isTwoSided`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean)
gives `(I * J).map f = I.map f * J.map f` whenever `I.map f` is two-sided.
The companion `Ideal.map_pow_of_isTwoSided` gives
`(I ^ n).map f = (I.map f) ^ n` for every natural exponent, including zero.
Neither semiring must be commutative, and `f` need not be surjective.

headlines.title: Annihilators after localization
headlines.text:
For commutative semirings `R`, `A`,
a submonoid `T : Submonoid R`, an `R`-algebra `A` realizing localization at
`T`, and a standard localized-module map `f : M →ₗ[R] N`,
[`IsLocalizedModule.map_annihilator`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/LocalizedModule.lean)
gives
```lean
Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) (Module.annihilator R M) =
  Module.annihilator A N
```
when `M` is finitely generated over `R`. The semimodules are additive
commutative monoids, `N` has its compatible `A`-action, and all four carrier
universes are independent. Zero semirings, zero modules and `0 ∈ T` are
allowed; no finite presentation, flatness or faithful-action assumption is
added. The supporting
[`IsLocalizedModule.comp_eq_iff_exists_smul_eq`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/LocalizedModule/Finite.lean)
characterizes equality after localization for two maps from a finitely
generated semimodule by a single submonoid multiplier making them equal.

headlines.title: Coatomicity of two-sided ideals
headlines.text:
For any unital, possibly nonassociative ring `R`,
[`TwoSidedIdeal.isCoatomic`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/TwoSidedIdeal/Atoms.lean)
proves `IsCoatomic (TwoSidedIdeal R)`: every proper two-sided ideal lies below a
maximal proper two-sided ideal. No nontriviality, commutativity or finiteness
assumption is needed. Use this theorem as a local instance with Mathlib's
coatom consumers. The
[simple-quotient example](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/TwoSidedIdeal.lean)
combines it with the congruence correspondence to obtain a nontrivial simple
quotient of an arbitrary nontrivial ring, with its surjective unital quotient map.

headlines.title: Radical colons and pointwise annihilators
headlines.text:
For a radical ideal `I` in a
commutative semiring `R` and an arbitrary subset `s : Set R`,
[`Ideal.IsRadical.colon`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Annihilator.lean)
proves `(I.colon s).IsRadical`; use it as `hI.colon s`.
Taking `I = ⊥` in a reduced commutative semiring shows that the ideal of
scalars `a` with `a * b = 0` for every `b ∈ s` is radical. No finiteness,
nonemptiness or nontriviality assumption is needed.

headlines.title: Finitely generated ideal colons and localization
headlines.text:
For commutative
semirings `R`, `S`, a submonoid `T : Submonoid R` and an `R`-algebra `S`
satisfying `[IsLocalization T S]`,
[`IsLocalization.comap_map_colon`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/Localization.lean)
gives
```lean
Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S)
    ((I.colon (J : Set R)).map (algebraMap R S)) =
  (Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S) (I.map (algebraMap R S))).colon (J : Set R)
```
for any ideal `I` and finitely generated ideal `J`, with
`Submodule.FG (J : Submodule R R)`. Thus multiplicative saturation, expressed
by extension followed by contraction, commutes with colon by `J`.
Finite generation concerns the ideal, not its underlying set. The two
universes are independent; zero semirings, `0 ∈ T`, `J = ⊥` and top ideals
are allowed. No finiteness or radicality of `I` is required.

headlines.title: Unit-ideal scalar families
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary family of scalars generating
the unit ideal in a semiring `S`,
[`Ideal.existsUnique_smul_eq_of_span_range_eq_top`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/Coprime.lean)
gives a unique common parameter for compatible elements of an `S`-semimodule
whose scalar actions commute. The index type need not be finite or nonempty,
and no subtraction or additive cancellation is needed.

headlines.title: Coprime scalar rows
headlines.text:
For a commutative semiring `S`, an additive
commutative `S`-semimodule `M`, and Bézout-coprime scalars `a`, `b`,
[`IsCoprime.existsUnique_smul_eq_pair`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/Coprime.lean)
gives a unique `k` with `a • k = x` and `b • k = y` whenever
`b • x = a • y`. The companion `smul_mem_range_smul_iff` reflects
membership in the range of multiplication by `a` after multiplying by `b`.
The two universes are independent; no subtraction, additive cancellation,
nontriviality or finiteness is assumed.

headlines.title: Finite coprime-kernel decompositions
headlines.text:
Let a commutative semiring `A` act through
a representation `τ : A →+* Module.End R M`, where `R` is any semiring and `M` is
an additive commutative `R`-semimodule. For a finite labelled pairwise Bézout-coprime
family `a`, the sole annihilation premise `τ (∏ i, a i) = 0` gives
[`RingHom.linearEquivPiKer`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/Coprime/Kernel.lean),
an explicit equivalence with the product of the labelled kernels. Its inverse sums
the kernel inclusions, and its projectors are independent of the whole Bézout
partition used to compute them. Empty families, zero semirings and noncommutative
scalar semirings are allowed; no subtraction or additive cancellation is needed.
Polynomial evaluation and scalar torsion decompositions are specializations.
Given a second such decomposition from `υ : B →+* Module.End T N` and a finite
family `b : J → B`, an arbitrary map `q : I → J` regroups the fine labels. An
additive map `h : M →+ N` intertwining each represented fibre-product
`τ (∏ i with q i = j, a i)` with `υ (b j)` intertwines the corresponding sum of
fine canonical projectors with the target projector; each target coordinate is
the fibre-sum of mapped fine coordinates. Empty fibres are allowed. The
coefficient and scalar semirings may differ; neither scalar-linearity nor
compatibility with other represented elements is required. Same-label
naturality is the specialization `q = id`.
The exact projector criterion is
[`RingHom.semiconj_sum_kerProjector_iff_mapsTo_ker`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/Coprime/Kernel.lean):
`h` intertwines all fibre-sums of fine projectors with the target projectors if
and only if it maps `ker (τ (a i))` into `ker (υ (b (q i)))` for every `i`.
This criterion requires no scalar-linearity or intertwining of represented
elements; its only annihilation premises are that both represented products
vanish. The eight coefficient, scalar, module and index universes are
independent. Both label sets are finite here because the canonical families
are finite.

headlines.title: Finite generation under pointwise unimodular clearing
headlines.text:
For arbitrary,
possibly noncommutative semirings `R`, `S` and `f : M →ₛₗ[φ] N` between
additive commutative left semimodules,
[`Submodule.fg_of_fg_comap_of_one_mem_span_smul_mem_range`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/Module/SpanRank.lean)
proves an `S`-submodule `P` finitely generated if `P.comap f` is finitely
generated over `R` and, for every `n ∈ P`, the clearers
`{a : S | ∃ m : M, f m = a • n}` generate the unit **left** ideal.
The companion `span_image_comap_eq_of_one_mem_span_smul_mem_range` identifies
`P` with the target-scalar span of its comap image without any finite-generation
premise. The existing single-left-inverse and unit-clearing criteria remain
specializations. The four universes are independent; neither Noetherianity
nor surjectivity of `φ` or `f` is required.

headlines.title: Semilinear Noetherian ascent
headlines.text:
For arbitrary semirings `R`, `S`, additive
commutative semimodules `M`, `N` and `f : M →ₛₗ[φ] N`,
[`isNoetherian_of_left_inv_smul_mem_range`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Noetherian.lean)
transfers `IsNoetherian R M` to `IsNoetherian S N` if each `n` admits
`m, a, b` with `b * a = 1` and `f m = a • n`. The four universes are
independent; neither `φ` nor `f` must be surjective. The
`isNoetherian_of_unit_smul_mem_range` corollary retains the familiar
unit-clearing hypothesis, while `isNoetherian_of_surjective_semilinear`
requires only function-surjectivity of `f`.

headlines.title: Artin–Rees for Noetherian modules
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary commutative ring `R`,
ideal `I` and submodule `K` of a Noetherian `R`-module `M`,
[`Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul_of_isNoetherian`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Filtration.lean)
gives a constant `c` such that
`(I ^ n • ⊤) ⊓ K = I ^ (n - c) • ((I ^ c • ⊤) ⊓ K)` for every `n ≥ c`.
Neither Noetherianity of `R` nor finite generation of `I` is assumed.
The ring and module universes are independent. The proof uses Mathlib's full
Artin–Rees theorem over the quotient by the module's annihilator. The
[shifted-cofinality client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Filtration.lean) uses
the full equality at Mathlib's Noetherian-ring and finite-module hypotheses.

headlines.title: Submodule adic cofinality
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary ideal `I` of a commutative
ring `R`,
[`Ideal.HasSubmoduleAdicCofinality`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicCompatibility.lean)
expresses `∀ n, ∃ m, N ⊓ (I ^ m • ⊤) ≤ I ^ n • N` for every submodule
`N` of every finite `R`-module. This is Fujiwara--Kato's (AP); restricting to
finitely generated submodules gives the existing
`Ideal.HasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality` condition (APf). Both `.cofinal`
eliminators allow an independent module universe. Nilpotent ideals satisfy
(AP) without Noetherianity or finite generation of the ideal or submodule;
every ideal of a Noetherian ring satisfies it by
[Artin–Rees](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Filtration.lean). The ambient module
need not be finitely presented. Cofinality is pointwise, not a full shifted
Artin–Rees equality. The APf providers follow from (AP), and the
[range client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Filtration.lean) applies the APf
API to maps between finite modules in independent universes.

headlines.title: Power-killed submodule criteria
headlines.text:
For an ideal `I` of a commutative ring `R`,
[`Ideal.hasSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_forall_exists_inf_pow_smul_eq_bot`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicCompatibility.lean)
characterizes (AP) by `∃ m, N ⊓ (I ^ m • ⊤) = ⊥` whenever
`∃ k, I ^ k • N = ⊥`, for every submodule `N` of every finite `R`-module.
The corresponding (APf) criterion tests only finitely generated `N`.
Both `.exists_inf_pow_smul_eq_bot` consumers allow an independent module
universe. A single common exponent kills the whole submodule; `I` need not
be finitely generated or nilpotent. The converse uses images in canonical
module quotients over the original coefficient ring `R`.

headlines.title: Descent of adic cofinality
headlines.text:
For commutative rings `R`, `A`,
[`Ideal.HasSubmoduleAdicCofinality.of_map_of_faithfullyFlat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicBaseChange.lean)
descends (AP) from `I.map (algebraMap R A)` to `I` along a faithfully flat
algebra. Alternatively,
[`Ideal.HasSubmoduleAdicCofinality.of_map_of_linearRetraction`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicBaseChange.lean)
uses an `R`-linear map `p : A →ₗ[R] R` with `p 1 = 1`, without a flatness
hypothesis; `p` need not preserve multiplication. Both have corresponding
`HasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality` methods for (APf). The algebra need not be
module-finite, the ideal need not be finitely generated, and no finite
presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is required. The pointwise
linear-retraction theorem works over commutative semirings and arbitrary
semimodules; its tensor membership and inclusion-reflection lemmas even
allow noncommutative scalar algebras. All carrier universes are independent.

headlines.title: Adic cofinality on finite products
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary ideal `I` of
`Π i, R i`, with `[Finite ι]` and commutative rings `R i`,
[`Ideal.hasSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_forall_map_evalRingHom`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicProducts.lean)
gives (AP) for `I` iff each projection image `I.map (Pi.evalRingHom R i)`
has (AP). The companion
`hasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_forall_map_evalRingHom` does the same
for (APf). The [characteristic criteria](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicProducts.lean)
also cover unary `Ideal.pi` and binary `Ideal.prod`, with independent binary
ring universes. Empty products and zero factors are allowed. Full (AP)
covers every submodule of every finite module; (APf) requires only the
submodule to be finitely generated. No ideal-FG, Noetherian or ambient
finite-presentation hypothesis is added. Infinite products are not covered
by these equivalences.

headlines.title: Cofinal ideal powers
headlines.text:
For ideals `I, J` of a commutative ring with
`I ^ a ≤ J` and `J ^ b ≤ I` for some natural numbers `a, b`,
[`Ideal.hasSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_of_pow_le`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicCompatibility.lean)
makes (AP) equivalent for `I` and `J`; the companion
`hasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_of_pow_le` does the same for (APf).
The witnesses may be zero. In particular, replacing an ideal by any positive
power preserves both conditions. The shared pointwise theorem
`Submodule.adic_cofinality_iff_of_pow_le` already applies to arbitrary left
ideals of a semiring and arbitrary submodules of an additive commutative
semimodule, with its given action and independent carrier universes.
This comparison needs no finiteness or additive-inverse hypothesis.

headlines.title: Semilinear transport of adic cofinality
headlines.text:
For semirings `R`, `S`, a
coefficient equivalence `σ : R ≃+* S` and a compatible semilinear
equivalence `e : M ≃ₛₗ[(σ : R →+* S)] P` between additive commutative
semimodules with their given actions,
[`Submodule.adic_cofinality_iff_of_semilinearEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicCompatibility.lean)
transports `∀ n, ∃ m, N ⊓ (I ^ m • ⊤) ≤ I ^ n • N` to the condition for
`I.map σ.toRingHom` and `N.map e.toLinearMap`. It allows arbitrary left
ideals and submodules in four independent universes, without finiteness
or additive inverses. For commutative rings, the companion
`Ideal.hasSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_of_ringEquiv` and
`Ideal.hasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_of_ringEquiv` give (AP)/(APf)
invariance under coefficient equivalence. Both predicates quantify over
finite ambient modules; only (APf) restricts submodules to be finitely
generated.

headlines.title: Stability of adic cofinality under scalar extension
headlines.text:
Over commutative
rings, both (AP) and (APf) pass from an ideal `I` to its extension
`I.map (algebraMap R A)` along a **module-finite** `R`-algebra `A`, or
along an arbitrary localization algebra. The localization algebra need not
be finite over `R`. The respective `.map` and `.map_of_isLocalization`
interfaces are in
[`AdicCompatibility`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicCompatibility.lean).
Neither ideal finite generation nor finite presentation or Noetherianity
is required; the original target action and independent carrier universes
are retained.

headlines.title: Adic cofinality near a closed locus
headlines.text:
For an ideal `I` of a commutative
ring `R` and any set `s : Set R` with `I ⊔ Ideal.span s = ⊤`, (AP) holds
for `I` if and only if it holds for every extension to `Localization.Away f`,
`f ∈ s`; the same equivalence holds for (APf). The
[`hasSubmoduleAdicCofinality_iff_forall_map_away` and finite-submodule counterpart](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicLocality.lean)
need only a distinguished-open cover of `V(I)`, not of the whole spectrum.
The set need not be finite. The ambient modules remain finite, with arbitrary
submodules for (AP) and finitely generated submodules for (APf); no ideal-FG,
ambient finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is added. Cutoffs are
pointwise, not a uniform shift or denominator bound, and this is not a
stalkwise criterion.

headlines.title: Krull intersection from adic cofinality
headlines.text:
For a finite module `M` and an
ideal `I` satisfying finite-submodule adic cofinality,
[`Ideal.HasFiniteSubmoduleAdicCofinality.mem_iInf_pow_smul_top_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicKrull.lean)
characterizes membership in `⨅ n, I ^ n • ⊤` by a scalar `a ∈ I` fixing
the element. The relative bound `I ≤ (Module.annihilator R M).jacobson`
makes this intersection zero. For any submodule `N` with finite quotient,
membership in `⨅ n, N ⊔ I ^ n • ⊤` is equivalent to
`(1 - a) • x ∈ N` for some `a ∈ I`; a Jacobson bound relative to the
quotient annihilator makes the intersection equal to `N`.
The ambient module and `N` need not be finite in the quotient statements.
No ideal-FG, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is added, and the
ring and module universes are independent. These are algebraic intersection
results, not assertions of topological closedness or completeness.

headlines.title: Finite generation from the first adic quotient
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary submodule
`N` of a finite original `R`-module `M`,
[`Submodule.fg_iff_finite_quotient_smul`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicKrull.lean)
detects `N.FG` on the intrinsic quotient `N / I N` over `R`, assuming APf and
`I ≤ (Module.annihilator R M).jacobson`. This is not the quotient by
`N ∩ I M`, and neither ideal-FG nor a Noetherian, finite-presentation,
flatness or completeness hypothesis is required.

headlines.title: Finite presentation from cofinal ideal quotients
headlines.text:
For a finite module `M`
over a commutative ring `R` and an ideal `I` satisfying full submodule adic
cofinality and `I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥`,
[`Ideal.finitePresentation_iff_forall_quotient_smul`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/AdicFinitePresentation.lean)
detects finite presentation over `R` on all reductions `M / J j M` over
`R / J j`, for any family `J : ι → Ideal R` with
`∀ n : ℕ, ∃ j, J j ≤ I ^ n`. The positive-powers criterion
`Ideal.finitePresentation_iff_forall_quotient_pow_smul` is a specialization.
The ring, module and index universes are independent; no ideal finite
generation or ordering condition on the family is required.

headlines.title: Essentially finite-type scalar extension
headlines.text:
For commutative rings `R`, `S`,
an essentially finite-type `R`-algebra structure on `S`, and a Noetherian
`R`-module `M`,
[`Algebra.EssFiniteType.isNoetherian_tensorProduct`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Noetherian.lean)
makes `S ⊗[R] M` Noetherian over `S` with its canonical left-factor action.
The three universes are independent, and `M` need only be an additive
commutative monoid with its given module structure. Neither ambient ring
must be Noetherian; no flatness, faithfulness or finite presentation is
assumed. This includes finite-type algebras and arbitrary localizations.

headlines.title: Coherent modules and kernels
headlines.text:
For a ring and an additive commutative monoid
with its given module structure, [`Module.IsCoherent`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Basic.lean)
means finite generation together with finite presentation of every finitely
generated submodule. [`Module.IsCoherent.iff_finite_and_fg_ker`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Basic.lean)
characterizes this by finitely generated kernels of *all* linear maps from
finite-rank free modules, including rank zero. The same leaf proves closure
under finitely generated submodules, finite products, kernels and cokernels,
quotients by finitely generated submodules, and extensions (with the stated
exactness and endpoint conditions). For rings `R` and `S`,
`Module.IsCoherent.of_restrictScalars` transfers coherence of an additive
commutative group `N` from `R` to `S` when `S` is finite over `R` and the given
module structures form scalar towers `R → S → S` and `R → S → N`.
No coherence of `S` over `R` is required, and the three universes are independent.

headlines.title: Coherent homology
headlines.text:
Over any possibly noncommutative `Ring R`, a three-term
complex `S : CategoryTheory.ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R)` with finite left
term `S.X₁` and coherent middle and right terms `S.X₂`, `S.X₃` has coherent
homology, by
[`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.isCoherent_homology`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/ModuleCat.lean).
The conclusion concerns the chosen categorical `S.homology` with its given
`R`-action. Neither the left term nor `R` is assumed coherent, and no exactness
hypothesis is imposed. The ring universe is independent of the common object
universe `v`.

headlines.title: Coherence along semilinear retractions
headlines.text:
For arbitrary rings `R`, `S` and
additive commutative monoids `N`, `M` with their given `R`- and `S`-module
structures, let `σ : R →+* S`, `τ : S →+* R`, `f : N →ₛₗ[σ] M` and
`g : M →ₛₗ[τ] N` satisfy `τ ∘ σ = id` and `g ∘ f = id`. Then
[`Module.IsCoherent.of_semilinear_retract`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Retraction.lean)
descends coherence of `M` over `S` to coherence of `N` over `R`. The four
carrier universes are independent; no additional scalar action, finiteness,
flatness, Noetherianity, faithfulness or nontriviality assumption is required.
The regular-module corollary `IsCoherentRing.of_retract` says that a ring
retract of a coherent ring is coherent, including noncommutative rings.

headlines.title: Coherent dependent direct sums
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary index type, a possibly
noncommutative ring `R`, and additive commutative monoids `M i` with their
given `R`-module structures,
[`Module.IsCoherent.directSum_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/DirectSum.lean)
gives
```lean
Module.IsCoherent R (DirectSum ι M) ↔
  (∀ i, Module.IsCoherent R (M i)) ∧ Set.Finite {i | ¬ Subsingleton (M i)}
```
Thus the nontrivial summands, not the ambient index type, must form a finite
set. Coherence means finite generation and finite presentation of every
finitely generated submodule. Empty index types, zero summands and zero
rings are allowed; no base-ring coherence, Noetherianity, faithfulness or
commutativity assumption is added. The index, ring and summand universes
are independent. `Module.IsCoherent.of_directSum` reflects coherence to
each original coordinate without a finite-index assumption. The supporting
[`Module.Finite.finite_nontrivial_summands`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/DirectSum.lean)
already obtains finiteness of the nontrivial summands from finite generation
over a semiring.

headlines.title: Coherence over product coefficient rings
headlines.text:
For any dependent family of
possibly noncommutative rings `R i` and additive commutative monoids `M i` with
their given `R i`-module structures,
[`Module.IsCoherent.of_piRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Pi.lean) reflects
coherence of the product to each coordinate. For `[Finite ι]`,
`Module.IsCoherent.piRing_iff` gives the converse as well:
```lean
Module.IsCoherent (∀ i, R i) (∀ i, M i) ↔
  ∀ i, Module.IsCoherent (R i) (M i)
```
The action is `(r • m) i = r i • m i`, with independently variable coordinate
scalars, not a common diagonal scalar ring. The index, coefficient and module
universes are independent. Reflection allows an arbitrary index type; the
equivalence requires only `[Finite ι]`. Empty products, zero rings and zero
modules are allowed. No Noetherianity, commutativity, faithfulness or extra
finite-generation hypothesis is assumed.
The regular-module specialization `isCoherentRing_pi_iff` characterizes
coherence of the product ring by coherence of every factor. Coherence of an
arbitrary coordinate module does not assert coherence of its coefficient ring.
The supporting [`Module.Finite.piRing_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Pi.lean)
proves the corresponding finite-generation equivalence already for semirings
and additive commutative monoids. These equivalences concern finite products;
coordinatewise coherence does not in general imply coherence of an infinite
product module over its product coefficient ring.

headlines.title: Finite presentation over product coefficient rings
headlines.text:
For any dependent family
of possibly noncommutative rings `R i` and additive commutative monoids `M i`
with their given `R i`-module structures,
[`Module.FinitePresentation.of_piRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Pi.lean)
reflects finite presentation of `Π i, M i` over `Π i, R i` to each coordinate.
This direction allows an arbitrary index type. For `[Finite ι]`,
`Module.FinitePresentation.piRing_iff` gives the converse as well:
```lean
Module.FinitePresentation (∀ i, R i) (∀ i, M i) ↔
  ∀ i, Module.FinitePresentation (R i) (M i)
```
The action is `(r • m) i = r i • m i`; the index, coefficient and module
universes are independent. No supplied additive group structure, coherence,
Noetherianity, commutativity or nontriviality is required. Empty products and
zero factors are allowed. The
[varying-rank client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/FinitePresentationPi.lean) combines
free modules over the integers and a noncommutative integer matrix ring.

headlines.title: Finite presentation along scalar towers
headlines.text:
For possibly noncommutative rings
`R`, `S` and an additive commutative monoid `N` with its given `R`- and
`S`-module structures and towers `R → S → S` and `R → S → N`,
[`Module.FinitePresentation.trans_of_tower`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FinitePresentation.lean)
gives finite presentation of `N` over `R` from finite presentation of `S`
over `R` and of `N` over `S`. Conversely, `of_restrictScalars` gives finite
presentation over `S` from finite presentation over `R` assuming only that
`S` is finite over `R`. Thus `restrictScalars_iff` equates the two finite-
presentation properties when `S` is finitely presented over `R`, without
assuming either property of `N` in advance. The three universes are
independent; no coherence, Noetherianity, centrality or faithfulness is
required. `trans_of_algebra` recovers the type and argument order of Mathlib's
commutative-algebra `Module.FinitePresentation.trans` as a corollary of the
scalar-tower theorem.

headlines.title: Coherence along quotient coefficients
headlines.text:
For possibly noncommutative rings
`R`, `S` and additive commutative monoids `N`, `M` with their given `R`- and
`S`-module structures,
[`Module.isCoherent_iff_of_bijective_of_fg_ker`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FinitePresentation.lean)
gives `Module.IsCoherent R N ↔ Module.IsCoherent S M` along a bijective
semilinear map `f : N →ₛₗ[σ] M`, provided `σ : R →+* S` is surjective and
`(RingHom.ker σ).FG`. Kernel finite generation is as a **left** ideal, not
merely as a two-sided ideal. The four carrier universes are independent;
`σ` need not be injective. No extra action, scalar inverse, coherence of an
ambient ring, Noetherianity, flatness or nontriviality hypothesis is required.

headlines.title: Coherence under scalar restriction
headlines.text:
For possibly noncommutative rings `R`
and `S`, if `S` is coherent as an `R`-module, then
[`Module.FinitePresentation.isCoherent_restrictScalars`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FinitePresentation.lean)
makes every finitely presented `S`-module `N` coherent for its given `R`-action.
The additive commutative group `N` has its given module structures and scalar
towers `R → S → S` and `R → S → N`; the three universes are independent.
Under these hypotheses, coherence over `R`, coherence over `S`, and finite
presentation over `S` are equivalent. No coherence assumption on `R`,
Noetherianity, centrality or faithfulness is required. The identity-scalar
specialization [`Module.isCoherent_iff_finitePresentation`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FinitePresentation.lean)
identifies the two properties over an `IsCoherentRing R`, yielding finite
presentation of kernels between finitely presented modules. The
[`of_exact_five` criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FinitePresentation.lean) gives finite
presentation of `M₃` in `M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → M₄ → M₅` when the sequence is exact
at `M₂`, `M₃`, `M₄`, `M₁` is finite, and `M₂`, `M₄`, `M₅` are finitely
presented. It requires neither endpoint injectivity nor surjectivity.

headlines.title: Localization and descent
headlines.text:
[`of_isLocalizedModule`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Localization.lean)
transports coherence along an arbitrary commutative-ring/module localization
realized by its universal property, not a surjective map. The
[`of_localizationSpan'` theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Localization.lean) descends
coherence from localizations away from a family whose ideal span is `⊤`.

headlines.title: Hom, tensor, and categories
headlines.text:
For semirings `R`, `R₂`, a ring `S`, and any
`σ : R →+* R₂`, [`Module.IsCoherent.semilinearMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Hom.lean)
makes `M →ₛₗ[σ] N` coherent over `S` when the additive commutative group `M`
is finitely presented over `R` and the additive commutative group `N` is
coherent over `S`, with commuting given `R₂`- and `S`-actions on `N`.
The five universes are independent and the Hom action is pointwise. No
`S`-action on `M`, `R`-action on `N`, scalar commutativity or surjectivity
of `σ` is required. The existing `linearMap` theorem is its same-base
commutative-ring specialization. For a commutative base ring `R` and an
independent, possibly noncommutative ring `S`,
[`tensorProduct_left`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/TensorProduct.lean) makes `M ⊗[R] N`
coherent over `S` when `M` is coherent over `S`, `N` is finitely presented
over `R`, and the given `R`- and `S`-actions on `M` commute. No `R`-module
structure on `S` or `S`-action on `N` is required. The existing `tensorProduct`
theorem retains the same-base, finitely-presented-first specialization.
These are theorems, not global instances, and assume neither
coherence nor Noetherianity of an ambient scalar ring.
[`CoherentModuleCat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/ModuleCat.lean) is a transparent full
subcategory with abelian structure obtained through generic category constructions.

headlines.title: Coherent right duals
headlines.text:
For a possibly noncommutative `Ring R` and a finitely
presented left `R`-module `M` with its given `AddCommMonoid` and module structure,
[`Module.FinitePresentation.isCoherent_dual`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Hom.lean) gives
`Module.IsCoherent Rᵐᵒᵖ (Module.Dual R M)` assuming only right coherence
`[IsCoherentRing Rᵐᵒᵖ]` of the ring. The dual uses the canonical right action
`(q • f) x = f x * MulOpposite.unop q` for `q : Rᵐᵒᵖ`, induced by right
multiplication on the codomain `R`. The ring and module universes are independent;
neither left coherence nor a supplied additive group structure on `M` is required.

headlines.title: Finite-module tensor zero detection
headlines.text:
For an arbitrary additive commutative
`R`-module `P` over a `CommRing R`,
[`Module.forall_maximal_smul_top_ne_top_iff_forall_finite_tensorProduct`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/FiniteDetection.lean)
characterizes zero-object detection on all finite modules by
`m • (⊤ : Submodule R P) ≠ ⊤` for every maximal ideal `m`.
[`Module.subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_of_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/FiniteDetection.lean)
gives `Subsingleton (P ⊗[R] M) ↔ Subsingleton M` for a single finite module
in an independent universe. No flatness, faithfulness or finiteness of `P`
is required. This detects zero objects, not zero maps or isomorphisms. The
[clients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/FiniteDetection.lean)
recover the finite faithfully-flat and local residue-field criteria and use
a countable direct sum of residue fields.

headlines.title: Ideal action on finite coefficients
headlines.text:
For an FG submodule `N` of an arbitrary
additive commutative module over a `CommRing R`,
[`Submodule.FG.ideal_smul_eq_self_iff_sup_annihilator_eq_top`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean)
says `I • N = N ↔ I ⊔ N.annihilator = ⊤` for every ideal `I`. For finite `P`,
[`Module.forall_maximal_smul_top_ne_top_iff_annihilator_le_jacobson`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean)
characterizes proper image under every maximal ideal by
`Module.annihilator R P ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥`, with no flatness or faithful-action
assumption. The [clients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean) recover
relative Jacobson properness and supply the finite tensor-detection input.

headlines.title: Semilinear invariance of flatness
headlines.text:
For equivalent commutative semirings
`e : R ≃+* S` and a compatible semilinear equivalence from an additive
commutative `R`-module `M` to an additive commutative `S`-module `N`,
[`Module.Flat.semilinearEquiv_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Equiv.lean)
gives `Module.Flat R M ↔ Module.Flat S N` for both given scalar actions.
`Module.Flat.of_semilinearEquiv e E` takes flatness of `N` to flatness of `M`.
The four carrier universes are independent. Over semirings, this is Mathlib's
mono-flatness (tensoring preserves injective linear maps); over rings it is
usual flatness. No faithful action, finiteness or additive cancellation is
required. The identity coefficient equivalence accepts the same ordinary
linear equivalence as Mathlib's fixed-ring flatness API.

headlines.title: Finiteness, projectivity and flatness under pure scalar extension
headlines.text:
Let `R : Type uR`
be a commutative ring, `S` an `R`-algebra and `M : Type uM` an additive
commutative monoid with its given `R`-module structure. Suppose the canonical
map `N → S ⊗[R] N`, `n ↦ 1 ⊗ n`, is injective for every additive commutative
`R`-semimodule `N : Type (max uR uM)`. Then
[`Module.Finite.iff_finite_tensorProduct_of_injective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Finiteness/Pure.lean)
gives `Module.Finite S (S ⊗[R] M) ↔ Module.Finite R M` for any `Semiring S`,
and
[`Module.FinitePresentation.iff_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_injective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Finiteness/Pure.lean)
gives the corresponding finite-presentation equivalence for any `Ring S`.
These scalar algebras need not be commutative. The
[submodule comparisons](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Submodule.lean)
reflect membership and inclusions and characterize finite generation of
scalar-extension images, without assuming tensoring preserves submodule
injections. If `S` is commutative,
[`Module.Flat.iff_flat_tensorProduct_of_injective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Pure.lean)
also gives `Module.Flat S (S ⊗[R] M) ↔ Module.Flat R M`.
The tensor has its canonical left-factor `S`-action; `M` needs no `S`-action
or supplied additive group structure. All three carrier universes are
independent. No flatness of `S` over `R` is assumed.
[`Module.finite_projective_of_tensorProduct_of_injective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Projective/Pure.lean)
descends finite projectivity for any possibly noncommutative `Semiring S`:
if `S ⊗[R] M` is finite and projective over `S`, then `M` is finite and
projective over `R`. Finite presentation of `M` is derived, not assumed.
The [clients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Finiteness/Pure.lean) also
retain the commutative-target proof using finitely presented flat modules
and apply the noncommutative result using a linear scalar retraction.

headlines.title: Annihilators under finite-limit-preserving scalar extension
headlines.text:
For a
`CommSemiring R`, a possibly noncommutative `Semiring S` with `Algebra R S`,
and a finitely generated semimodule `M`,
[`Module.annihilator_tensorProduct_eq_map_of_finite_of_preservesFiniteLimits`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
gives
```lean
Module.annihilator S (S ⊗[R] M) =
  Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (Module.annihilator R M)
```
provided the stock `SemimoduleCat` tensor-left functor for the lifted `S`
preserves finite limits over the lifted `R`, at the common universe
`max uR (max uS uM)`. The conclusion uses the original `S` and original tensor
product; the three original universes are independent. Here finite means
`Module.Finite R M`, not a finite carrier. No additive cancellation,
subtractivity, faithful action, finite presentation or Noetherianity is
required. This condition is not identified with mono-flatness over semirings.
Over commutative rings, flatness supplies this condition through the existing
module–semimodule equivalence. For any module `M` over a commutative ring `R`
and a flat, possibly noncommutative `R`-algebra `S`,
[`Module.annihilator_tensorProduct_eq_iInf_map_of_flat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
identifies the annihilator of `S ⊗[R] M` with the intersection of the ideals
generated by the images of `Module.annihilator R N`, over all finitely
generated original submodules `N ≤ M`. This is not a claim that ideal
extension commutes with arbitrary intersections. For finite `M`,
[`Module.annihilator_tensorProduct_eq_map_of_finite_of_flat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
identifies it with the ideal generated by `Module.annihilator R M` itself.
The tensor has its canonical left-factor action; `M` needs no `S`-action.
`S` need only be a semiring and `M` an additive commutative monoid with the
given structures. The three universes are independent. No Noetherianity,
finite presentation, flatness or faithfulness of `M`, or faithful flatness
of `S` is required. The [clients](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
evaluate the intersection for the nonfinite free abelian group `ℕ →₀ ℤ`
after rational scalar extension and recover finite faithful-action
preservation over ring coefficients. The existing
`FaithfulSMul.baseChange_of_finite_of_flat` additionally allows commutative
semiring coefficients.

headlines.title: Annihilator contraction under faithfully flat extension
headlines.text:
Over a `CommRing R`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.annihilator_tensorProduct_eq`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/TensorProduct.lean)
says tensoring an arbitrary `R`-module `M` with a faithfully flat module `P`
preserves its annihilator over `R`. Here `P` is only a module group, while `M`
needs only an additive commutative monoid structure. For a faithfully flat,
possibly noncommutative ring algebra `S`,
[`Module.comap_annihilator_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
identifies contraction of the annihilator of `S ⊗[R] M` with the original
annihilator. The tensor has its canonical left-factor action and `M` needs no
`S`-action. All three carrier universes are independent, with no finiteness,
flatness or faithfulness assumption on `M`. The
[module client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Flat/TensorProduct.lean) derives
preservation and reflection of faithful action over the coefficient ring;
this does not assert faithful action over a larger scalar algebra.

headlines.title: Faithfully flat tensor products
headlines.text:
Over a `CommRing R`, for additive
commutative groups `C` and `D` with `R`-module structures,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.tensorProduct_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/TensorProduct.lean)
says that `C ⊗[R] D` is faithfully flat over `R` if and only if both `C` and
`D` are faithfully flat over `R`. The ring and the two module universes are
independent; no finiteness, projectivity or nontriviality assumption is needed.

headlines.title: Faithfully flat dependent direct sums
headlines.text:
For arbitrary families of additive
commutative groups with module structures over a `CommRing R`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.directSum_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/DirectSum.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness of the direct sum by flatness of every
component and a nontrivial quotient-tensor fiber in some component for each
proper ideal of `R`. The detecting component may depend on the ideal; the
components need not individually be faithfully flat. The ring, index and
carrier universes are independent, and empty indexing types are allowed.
One faithfully flat component is sufficient when every component is flat.

headlines.title: Finitely generated ideals and dependent products
headlines.text:
Over a `CommSemiring R`,
[`Submodule.smul_pi_of_fg`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/LinearAlgebra/Pi.lean) says that
multiplication by a finitely generated ideal commutes with the full dependent
product of submodules of additive commutative `R`-modules. The index type is
arbitrary, including empty, and the semiring, index and carrier universes are
independent.

headlines.title: Faithful flatness after base change covering maximal ideals
headlines.text:
For commutative
rings `R` and `S` with an `R`-algebra structure on `S`, suppose every maximal
ideal `m` of `R` satisfies `m.map (algebraMap R S) ≠ ⊤`. For any additive
commutative group `M` with an `R`-module structure,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_baseChange_of_map_maximal_ne_top`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness over `R` by **original** flatness `Module.Flat R M`
and faithful flatness over `S` of `S ⊗[R] M`, with the canonical left tensor-factor
action. The three universes are independent. No flatness of `S` over `R`,
surjectivity, algebra structure on `M`, finiteness, Noetherianity, localness,
topology or completion is assumed. For `I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_baseChange_of_le_jacobson`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat.lean)
specializes this to the canonical quotient `R ⧸ I`. For commutative
`R`-algebras `S`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_quotient_of_le_jacobson`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat.lean)
gives the equivalent formulation using the canonical quotient algebra
`R ⧸ I → S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S)`. Conversely,
[`Algebra.map_maximal_ne_top_iff_forall_faithfullyFlat_baseChange`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/BaseChange.lean)
characterizes the maximal-ideal hypothesis itself: it holds **if and only if**
scalar extension preserves and reflects faithful flatness for every originally
flat `R`-module in `Type (max u w)`, where `R : Type u` and `w` is arbitrary.
The universe of `S` remains independent. The converse uses the direct sum of
principal localizations indexed by all elements of a maximal ideal, without
assuming that ideal is finitely generated. The
[quotient client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat.lean)
applies this corollary to the nonsurjective rank-two diagonal over `ZMod 4`
with the proper nonzero square-zero ideal `(2)`. Its inputs are obtained
independently from basis-derived faithful flatness.

headlines.title: Faithful flatness of unital algebras
headlines.text:
For a `CommRing R` and a unital
`R`-algebra `A` whose underlying ring may be noncommutative,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.algebra_iff_flat_and_fg_proper_ideal`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness by flatness and
`I • (⊤ : Submodule R A) ≠ ⊤` for every finitely generated proper ideal `I`.
The algebra structure is material; this finitely generated ideal criterion
is not asserted for arbitrary modules.

headlines.title: Faithfully flat products of algebras
headlines.text:
Over a `CommRing R`, for an arbitrary
dependent family of unital, possibly noncommutative `R`-algebras `A i`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_algebra_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Pi.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness of `Π i, A i` by flatness of the **whole
product** and a nontrivial fiber `(R ⧸ I) ⊗[R] A i` in some component for
every finitely generated proper ideal `I`. The detecting component may depend
on the ideal. Componentwise flatness cannot replace whole-product flatness,
and the components need not individually be faithfully flat. The ring, index
and carrier universes are independent, and empty products are allowed.

headlines.title: Products of localizations at submonoids
headlines.text:
For a `CommRing R`, arbitrary
submonoids `S i` and commutative `R`-algebras `A i` realizing the localizations
at `S i`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_localization_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Localization.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness of `Π i, A i` by flatness of the **whole
product** and, for every finitely generated proper ideal `I`, disjointness
of `I` from some `S i`. These are products with the common diagonal `R`-action;
neither finite nor nonempty indexing is required, and zero rings are allowed.

headlines.title: Families of principal localizations
headlines.text:
For a `CommRing R` and any family
`s : ι → R`,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.directSum_away_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Localization.lean)
characterizes faithful flatness of `⨁ i, Localization.Away (s i)` by
`Ideal.span (Set.range s) = ⊤`, without finite or nonempty indexing.
For **finite** index types,
[`Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_away_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Flat/Localization.lean)
gives the same unit-span criterion for `Π i, Localization.Away (s i)`.
The localizations need not individually be faithfully flat; zero rings and
independent ring and index universes are allowed. The finite-index hypothesis
for the product unit-span criterion is essential: the
[coordinate-idempotent product](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Flat/LocalizationProductInfinite.lean)
is faithfully flat although its generators span a proper ideal. The
[ideal-detection consequences](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Flat/LocalizationProductCriteria.lean)
show that this ideal is not finitely generated.

headlines.title: Faithfully flat coherence descent
headlines.text:
