[`Module.IsCoherent.of_isCoherent_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FaithfullyFlatDescent.lean)
descends coherence of the canonical scalar extension `S ⊗[R] M` to the original
module `M`. The scalar algebra `S` may be noncommutative; no finiteness hypothesis
on `M` or module-finiteness of `S` is needed. The regular-module consequence
[`IsCoherentRing.of_faithfullyFlat`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/FaithfullyFlatDescent.lean)
descends ring coherence. The original module's additive monoid and action are
retained, with independent ring, algebra and module universes.

headlines.title: Universal coherence
headlines.text:
[`IsUniversallyCoherent`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/UniversallyCoherent.lean)
asserts coherence for finitely presented commutative algebras in an independently
chosen target universe; the library derives base coherence at `v = u` and
supplies the Noetherian case. Finitely presented algebra extensions preserve universal
coherence with independent base, extension and target universes. In particular, polynomial
rings over universally coherent rings are universally coherent; no module-finiteness
hypothesis is needed. Coherence of all finite-variable polynomial rings characterizes
universal coherence at the base-ring universe and implies universal coherence in every
independently chosen target universe. In particular, base-universe universal coherence
suffices for arbitrary target universes; no converse from an arbitrary smaller target
universe is asserted. Polynomial rings in an arbitrary type of variables over a
base-universe universally coherent ring are universally coherent, with independent
variable and target universes; neither finitely many variables nor a Noetherian base is
required. Arbitrary localizations of base-universe universally coherent rings are
universally coherent, with independent localization and target universes. No finite
denominator family or algebra finite-presentation hypothesis on the localization is needed.

headlines.title: Associative square-zero multiplication
headlines.text:
For a type `R` with multiplication and an
additive monoid `M` with distributive left and right actions,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.mul_assoc_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Associativity.lean)
characterizes associativity by coefficient associativity, composition of each action
(in reversed coefficient order on the right), and commutation of the two actions.
Addition need not commute, the carrier universes are independent, and no coefficient
zero, one, or identity law for either action is required.

headlines.title: Commutativity of square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
For `Mul R`, `AddZeroClass M`,
`IsAddCommutative M`, and two given zero-preserving scalar actions
`[SMulZeroClass R M]` and `[SMulZeroClass Rᵐᵒᵖ M]`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.isMulCommutative_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Commutativity.lean)
characterizes `IsMulCommutative (TrivSqZeroExt R M)` by
`IsMulCommutative R ∧ IsCentralScalar R M`. It retains the original
multiplication, addition, zero and both actions, with independent carrier
universes. No additive associativity, coefficient zero or one, module structure,
action compatibility or finiteness is required. This is a criterion for the
multiplication alone, not an assertion of a unit or a square-zero ideal at
these hypotheses.

headlines.title: Square-zero kernels and projection base change
headlines.text:
For a commutative semiring
`R` and an additive commutative `R`-module `M`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.kerIdealLinearEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Finite.lean)
identifies the projection kernel with `M`. If `M` is finite over `R`,
[`kerIdeal_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Finite.lean) makes the
kernel finite over the **whole extension**.
[`kerIdealBaseChange`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Finite.lean)
identifies the projection-base-changed kernel with `M` **without** a finiteness
assumption; its pure-tensor and inverse formulas are simp lemmas.

headlines.title: Full left-ideal lattice of square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
For a possibly
noncommutative division semiring `D : Type u` and an additive commutative group
`M : Type v` with its given actions `[Module D M]`, `[Module Dᵐᵒᵖ M]` and
`[SMulCommClass D Dᵐᵒᵖ M]`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.idealOrderIsoWithTop`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Ideal.lean)
identifies `Ideal (TrivSqZeroExt D M)` with `WithTop (Submodule D M)` as ordered
lattices. The two carrier universes are independent. A coefficient submodule
`N` corresponds to `0 × N`, using the original left action. The adjoined top
is the whole extension, whereas the coerced internal top is the proper
projection kernel
`K = RingHom.ker (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom ℕ D M : TrivSqZeroExt D M →+* D)`,
even when `M` is zero. The
[coatom client](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Ideal.lean) derives
maximality of this kernel through the order isomorphism. No ring structure on
`D`, centrality or finiteness assumption is required. Coefficient submodules
can be cones rather than additive subgroups and need not be stable under the
right action; this classifies **left** ideals, not only two-sided ideals.

headlines.title: Module length and square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
For modules over arbitrary rings,
[`LinearMap.length_eq_of_bijective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Length.lean)
preserves length under a bijective semilinear map whose scalar homomorphism is
surjective, without requiring that scalar homomorphism to be injective. The
rings and modules have four independent universes, and infinite lengths are
included. Its [algebra-map specialization](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModulesTest/RingTheory/Length.lean)
recovers Mathlib's surjective-algebra comparison under the same hypotheses.
For a division ring `D` and the original compatible left/right actions on `M`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.length`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Length.lean)
computes the regular left-module length as `Module.length D M + 1`, directly
from the ideal-lattice classification. Only the finrank corollary adds
`[Module.Finite D M]`; neither centrality nor right-finiteness is assumed.

headlines.title: Coherent square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
Over an arbitrary division ring `D`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.isCoherentRing_iff_finite_of_divisionRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Coherent.lean)
characterizes left coherence of `TrivSqZeroExt D M` by `Module.Finite D M`,
retaining both given compatible bimodule actions without centrality. The module
may be zero, and the two carrier universes are independent. The canonical-field
specialization
[`TrivSqZeroExt.isCoherentRing_iff_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Coherent.lean)
retains its given left action and canonical opposite action; finite generation
is equivalently finite dimension, not a finite underlying set. More generally,
`TrivSqZeroExt.finite_of_isCoherentRing_of_injective_smul` deduces left finite
generation from left coherence of an extension with its given compatible
bimodule actions and a vector `v` such that `r ↦ r • v` is injective.
The base ring may be noncommutative and the right action need not be central.
The existing `TrivSqZeroExt.isCoherentRing` gives sufficiency for a left
coherent base and a coefficient bimodule finitely presented on the left.
For the stock pointwise left module `ι →₀ D` and any given compatible right
module, [`TrivSqZeroExt.isCoherentRing_finsupp_iff_finite`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Finsupp.lean)
identifies left coherence with `Finite ι`, including the empty index type.
For a field `k` and infinite `ι`,
[`TrivSqZeroExt.finsupp_faithfullyFlat_and_not_isCoherentRing`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Finsupp.lean)
gives a faithfully flat, noncoherent `k`-algebra: the canonical idealization
`TrivSqZeroExt k (ι →₀ k)` with inclusion `a ↦ (a, 0)` and coordinatewise
scalar action. Faithful flatness follows from freeness and the nontrivial
field coordinate; it does not require the coefficient module to be faithfully flat.

headlines.title: Opposites of square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
[`TrivSqZeroExt.opEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Opposite.lean)
identifies `(TrivSqZeroExt R M)ᵐᵒᵖ` with `TrivSqZeroExt Rᵐᵒᵖ M` by
`op (r, m) ↦ (op r, m)`. The target uses the original right action on the
left and the original left action pulled back by double `unop` on the right.
The equivalence needs only `Add R`, `Mul R`, `AddCommMagma M`, and the two
given scalar actions. For a division ring `D` and an `AddCommGroup M` with
commuting bimodule actions, the double-opposite module is
`Module.compHom M (RingEquiv.opOp D).symm.toRingHom`. The preceding left
criterion and coherence transport then give the right-coherence criterion
`IsCoherentRing ((TrivSqZeroExt D M)ᵐᵒᵖ) ↔ Module.Finite Dᵐᵒᵖ M`,
with finiteness measured using the original right action, without centrality
or a comparison of left and right dimensions.

headlines.title: Left Noetherian square-zero extensions
headlines.text:
For a possibly noncommutative
`Ring R` and an `AddCommMonoid M` with commuting left and right `R`-module
actions, [`TrivSqZeroExt.isNoetherianRing_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/Algebra/TrivSqZeroExt/Noetherian.lean)
characterizes `IsNoetherianRing (TrivSqZeroExt R M)` by
`IsNoetherianRing R ∧ Module.Finite R M`. Finiteness here is as a **left**
`R`-module. The companion `TrivSqZeroExt.isNoetherianRing_iff_isNoetherian`
replaces `Module.Finite R M` by `IsNoetherian R M`. Centrality is not required,
and the two carrier universes are independent.

headlines.title: Finite-type ideal/module transfer
headlines.text:
Over a commutative base ring,
[`Ideal.ideal_property_iff_module_property`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/CoherentModules/RingTheory/Ideal/FiniteModuleTransfer.lean)
equates a property on all finitely generated ideals with one on all finite
modules over finite-type algebras. The property must be invariant under
compatible algebra/module isomorphisms and descend along **every** compatible
surjective square-zero algebra map for finite source modules. The base universe
is independent of the common algebra/module universe. Finite type does not
mean module-finite over the base, and arbitrary ideals need not be finitely
generated.

The foundation, finite-presentation and coherent-module category results allow
arbitrary `Ring`. Coherent semilinear Hom allows arbitrary source and target
scalar `Semiring`s with a commuting `Ring` action on the target. Localization
of coherent modules and universal coherence use `CommRing`. Coherent tensor closure
uses a `CommRing` base but allows an independent, possibly noncommutative `Ring`
acting on the coherent factor.
The square-zero commutativity criterion uses only `Mul`, `AddZeroClass`,
`IsAddCommutative` and the two given `SMulZeroClass` actions. The square-zero
kernel and base-change results use `CommSemiring` and `AddCommMonoid`; the
full left-ideal classification uses `DivisionSemiring` and `AddCommGroup` with
both given commuting module actions. The square-zero Noetherian criterion allows
`Ring` and `AddCommMonoid` with commuting bimodule actions. The coherent-extension
sufficiency and injective-vector necessity use `Ring` and `AddCommGroup`, without
centrality. The finite-generation
biconditional uses an arbitrary division ring and the given compatible bimodule
with `AddCommGroup`; its canonical-field specialization gives finite dimensionality.
The predicate transfer uses `CommRing` and `AddCommGroup`.
The ideal/product identity and semilinear mono-flatness invariance use
`CommSemiring` and `AddCommMonoid`; the faithful-flatness criteria use `CommRing`
and require no coherence or projectivity assumption. Module carrier universes are independent where stated.
Zero rings/modules, empty indexing sets and rank-zero finite free
modules are not excluded. Consult the linked source statements and
[guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/coherent-modules/blob/b670b34e8741624c22b88375b9086d6d393cbbc3/docs/Guide.md) for exact hypotheses. This is not a coherent-sheaf theory
or a claim to formalize an entire source.
